name: These Arms Are Snakes
label: Jade Tree
lede: [[Botch]] ended in 2002, and its bassist, [[Brian Cook]], started a Seattle band with a name its members thought sounded ridiculous. Four drummers, a van that met a semi-truck and a winter on tour with Underoath later, it ended when the gear gave out at the last show.

eras.title: After Botch, something stranger
eras.text: Botch broke up in 2002, and bassist Brian Cook started a Seattle band almost at once. He pulled in Steve Snere from Kill Sadie, Ryan Frederiksen from Nineironspitfire, drummer Joe Preston and keyboardist Jesse Robertson, and gave it a name they thought sounded ridiculous.

years.h: [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]] splits, and its bassist already has a next band
years.p: The breakup follows friction between drummer Tim Latona and guitarist Dave Knudson, and Botch plays its last show on June 15, 2002 at the Showbox in Seattle. Brian Cook is already on to something else.

years.src: Wikipedia: These Arms Are Snakes · Noisey
years.h: Five players, and a name that sounds like no other band
years.p: Steve Snere, Ryan Frederiksen, Brian Cook, Joe Preston and Jesse Robertson start These Arms Are Snakes in Seattle. Bill Quinby plays guitar for 2002 only.
years.xp:
They picked the name, the band said, because it was "ridiculous and [didn't] really sound like any other band name that's out there."

The members came from three Seattle bands: Cook from [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]], Snere from [[Kill Sadie|1b2717df-9eea-423b-8ee6-6d678d0cd35a]] and Frederiksen from Nineironspitfire. Before the debut EP they cut a four-song demo that stayed unreleased for twenty years.

years.h: This Is Meant to Hurt You opens the catalog on Jade Tree
years.p: It's the only release with Robertson as a full-time keyboardist. AllMusic gives it three stars and calls the lyrics smart and cunning.

eras.title: A semi-truck and the Totally Badical Tour
eras.text: Two members left in two years, and the drummer's farewell ended with the van meeting a semi-truck. A four-piece made Oxeneers, then spent a winter opening for Underoath.

years.h: Jesse Robertson leaves over how the band tours
years.p: The keyboardist disagrees with the others about touring and goes. As a four-piece, the band writes sparer arrangements and gets more room to move around the stage.

years.h: A van, a semi-truck and Joe Preston's last night
years.p: Preston plays his farewell show, and the van carrying him and the rest of the band collides with a semi-truck afterward. Erin Tate, of [[Kill Sadie|1b2717df-9eea-423b-8ee6-6d678d0cd35a]] and [[Minus the Bear|c1e98e4a-4628-4c89-a7a6-0e0171600b05]], takes over the drums.
years.xp: Wikipedia records the crash but not where it happened or who was hurt. Tate had played with Snere in Kill Sadie; he drums on the debut album Oxeneers and stays until 2005.

years.h: Like a Virgin puts the band next to Harkonen
years.p: Hydra Head and Mind Over Matter release the split, which includes a joint track called Touched for the Very First Time.

years.h: Oxeneers comes with a hidden track after Idaho
years.p: [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]] co-produces at Litho and Spectre South, and Tate drums. Jade Tree issues the CD and Second Nature the vinyl; Pitchfork gives it 7.6.
years.xp: The untitled piece starts at 6:36 of Idaho. Bayles also plays extra guitar and percussion, and Ben Verellen and Botch's Dave Knudson are among the guests.

years.cap: These Arms Are Snakes live, May 2005
years.h: On Underoath's Totally Badical Tour, the Snakes are the odd band out
years.p: The bill also has The Chariot, Hopesfall and Fear Before the March of Flames, and the crowds are cool. Underoath's members, openly Christian, keep clashing with the band over religion and politics.
years.xp:
The band said selling merch on the tour felt like an empty gesture.

The arguments about faith outlasted the tour. They fed loosely into the themes of the next album, Easter.

years.h: Ben Verellen quits without a word, and Chris Common takes over
years.p: Tate leaves, Verellen joins as drummer and walks out with no explanation, and [[Chris Common|680f3d25-dc62-4f1d-a5e4-6c56f785287d]] steps in. A producer as well as a drummer, Common stays through 2009 and makes the next two albums.

eras.title: An album called Easter
eras.text: With Chris Common on drums, the band made Easter, a record that circles religion after a tour spent arguing about it. Then it went back out, from Thrice's bills to Mastodon's.

years.h: The Good Friday 7-inch is a first for Suicide Squeeze
years.p: The band also gives Old Paradise to the label's Slaying Since 1996 compilation.

years.h: Easter picks up the religion argument
years.p: Common and the band produce, with [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]] engineering. Religion runs through it, Perpetual Bris most plainly, though the band said it wasn't making a public statement about organized religion.
years.xp:
Snere said he was writing about the bigger picture of life and existence. The friction with Underoath on the Totally Badical Tour loosely shaped the record's direction.

Cook and Demian Johnston made the artwork. The Jade Tree catalog number is JT1118.

years.h: Easter goes on the road with Thrice and Young Widows
years.p: The fall run also has [[Planes Mistaken for Stars|ff428f12-1c80-4437-bfff-0e9af6ff94c9]] and Mouth of the Architect on the bill.

years.cap: These Arms Are Snakes live, May 2007
years.h: Headliners in Europe, openers for Mastodon at home
years.p: After a European headline run, the band opens for [[Against Me!|a66ebddc-ff04-46b8-820a-15c63e80dba1]] and [[Mastodon|bc5e2ad6-0a4a-4d90-b911-e9a7e6861727]].

years.h: Cook takes a second bass job, in Russian Circles
years.p: He joins the Chicago instrumental band [[Russian Circles|cca40a67-e959-46f8-a3f3-8a3f77d2da9e]] while still a Snake, a double life that will shape how the band ends.
years.xp: Cook later told Noisey: "At the time, I was already juggling Russian Circles and These Arms Are Snakes."

eras.title: A last album, a bad night
eras.text: The band moved from Jade Tree to Suicide Squeeze, cut its final album in a month and scattered songs across splits with friends. Then it ended, faster than anyone had planned.

years.cap: These Arms Are Snakes on stage, September 2008
years.h: Pelican, Russian Circles and Tropics each get a split
years.p: The records come out on Hydra Head, Sargent House and We-Be. Frederiksen also starts [[Narrows|3a9bf775-66f1-4299-b062-5cb0585d5672]] with Botch singer Dave Verellen.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the limited-edition 12-inch with Russian Circles was put out on tour in 2008.

years.h: Tail Swallower and Dove is made in a month at Red Room
years.p: It's the fastest album the band makes, cut with Common. The band praises Suicide Squeeze's marketing and a roster of friends like [[Minus the Bear|c1e98e4a-4628-4c89-a7a6-0e0171600b05]].
years.xp: The third and final album moves away from the band's hardcore roots toward stranger textures and more traditional song shapes. Pitchfork gave it 6.4.

years.cap: These Arms Are Snakes on stage, June 2009
years.h: A limited split 7-inch on Touch and Go is the last new release
years.p: All the Saints share the record. Nothing new comes out while the band is still a band.

years.big: "Our gear kind of crapped out and that was it."
years.src: Noisey · Wikipedia: These Arms Are Snakes
years.h: The band announces its end on Christmas Day
years.p: Brian Cook on the final show. The band had been planning to start a fourth album that December.
years.xp:
Cook told Noisey the end was abrupt, with Russian Circles pulling on him at the same time. The last show was unceremonious, and the farewell shows the band talked about never happened.

Asked if he was satisfied with how it ended, Cook said "Not really."

eras.title: The songs left in the drawer
eras.text: Unreleased recordings kept surfacing after the breakup, and the band played Seattle twice more.

years.h: Their Nirvana cover of Heart-Shaped Box finally gets out
years.p: Shelved since the breakup, it appears on Robotic Empire's In Utero, in Tribute, in Entirety for Record Store Day.

years.h: A Lost Sounds cover, meant for a split that never happened, comes out
years.p: Energy Drink and the Long Walk Home was recorded for a Minus the Bear split. Suicide Squeeze puts it out on a split with [[The Coathangers|60698f82-b047-48a4-8612-8e9bde5b5fd4]] instead.
years.xp: Cook told Noisey it was among the last unreleased recordings in the vault, along with an old four-song demo of different versions of songs from the first EP.

years.src: BrooklynVegan · Wikipedia: These Arms Are Snakes
years.h: A secret show at Barboza, with the 2005 drummer back behind the kit
years.p: The band plays with Constant Lovers, Merso and Dust Moth. On drums is Ben Verellen, the drummer who quit without a word in 2005.
years.xp: BrooklynVegan called it a short surprise performance, teased on Facebook beforehand. It noted that Verellen, of Helms Alee, drummed the way he had in 2005.

years.h: Second reunion show, this time announced ahead
years.p: The band plays Seattle twelve years after the breakup. A fan multicam of the full set is on YouTube.

years.h: Duct Tape & Shivering Crows clears out the vault
years.p: Suicide Squeeze collects split tracks, compilation songs and the four-song demo recorded before This Is Meant to Hurt You. The same year, Cook's old band [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]] reunites.
